fieldMappings.transform: Take the last non-empty segment of `url` (e.g. https://swapi.dev/api/people/1/ -> "1"). Never store the URL as the id.
fieldMappings.notes: Provider has no explicit id field; the URL is the only stable identifier.

fieldMappings.transform: Parse as invariant integer; "unknown", empty or unparsable -> null.
Remove thousands separators (","), parse as invariant double; "unknown", empty or unparsable -> null.
fieldMappings.notes: Jabba's mass is "1,358" — separator must be stripped, not treated as a decimal point.

fieldMappings.transform: Match /^(\d+(\.\d+)?)(BBY|ABY)$/ case-insensitively; BBY -> negative, ABY -> positive; "unknown" or no match -> null.
fieldMappings.notes: Product says negative = before Battle of Yavin, but does not say whether 0BBY/0ABY both map to 0 or whether unparsable values should be null or throw. Calendar semantics are a business decision.

fieldMappings.transform: Case-insensitive lookup: male -> Male, female -> Female, hermaphrodite -> Other, unknown -> Unknown. "n/a" is ambiguous (see unresolvedQuestions).
fieldMappings.notes: "n/a" is what SWAPI uses for droids. Whether a droid is Other (has a value, not in the binary) or Unknown (no data) changes downstream filters.

fieldMappings.transform: Split on ",", trim each, drop empty; "n/a" and "none" -> empty list.
Last non-empty path segment of the homeworld URL; null/empty -> null.
Map each URL to its last non-empty path segment, preserving order; null -> empty list.
Copy `edited` converted to UTC; null -> null. (`created` is ignored.)
fieldMappings.notes: `edited` is the closer semantic match for 'last modified'.

unresolvedQuestions: gender: does "n/a" (droids) map to Other or to Unknown?
birthYear: should an unparsable non-"unknown" value (e.g. "12BBY?") be null, or should the record be rejected as invalid_response?

decisions.gender: "n/a" -> Other. Droids are a real category, not missing data. Only "unknown" and unrecognised values -> Unknown.
decisions.birthYear: Unparsable non-"unknown" values -> null. Bad calendar data must never fail a lookup.
